stemBlocks.value: Q = (2  -1 / 4  3), R = (1  6 / -5  4) and S = (2  7 / 4  -1 / -8  9), a 3x2 matrix. (i) Explain why the matrix product QS is NOT possible. (ii) State the order of the matrix product SR. (iii) Calculate the matrix product QR. (b) Given A = (4  -1 / -7  x), determine the value of x when the determinant of A is 5.
Think first: Write the order of every matrix beside it first; the conformability questions then answer themselves.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p295-q06 from workbook page 295.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write down the order of each matrix.

contentBlocks.value: Q is 2x2, R is 2x2, S is 3x2 (three rows, two columns).
Q has 2 columns but S has 3 rows, and 2 is not equal to 3.

solutionSteps.instruction: Test SR and give the order of the product.

contentBlocks.value: S is 3x2 and R is 2x2; the inner numbers both equal 2, so the product exists and takes the outer numbers 3 and 2.

solutionSteps.instruction: Multiply Q by R, row into column.
For (b), write the determinant of A and set it equal to 5.

strategyBlocks.value: Compare the inner dimensions for QS and SR, multiply Q by R row into column, and set the determinant expression for A equal to 5.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) QS is not possible because Q has 2 columns while S has 3 rows; for multiplication the number of columns of the first matrix must equal the number of rows of the second.  (ii) SR is of order 3x2.  (iii) QR = (7  8 / -11  36)  (b) x = 3

whyThisWorks.value: Each entry of a product pairs a whole row of the first matrix with a whole column of the second, so those two lists must be the same length; that is the conformability rule, and it also explains why the product keeps the rows of the first matrix and the columns of the second. The determinant of a 2x2 matrix is the product of the leading diagonal minus the product of the other diagonal, and careful sign work with the two negative entries is what makes -(-1)(-7) come out as -7.

commonErrors.misconception: Reading S as 2x3 instead of 3x2 and claiming QS is possible.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Reading S as 2x3 instead of 3x2 and claiming QS is possible.

commonErrors.misconception: Answering (i) with 'the matrices are different sizes' rather than naming the columns and rows that fail to match.

commonErrors.misconception: Getting the sign of (-1)(-7) wrong in the determinant and writing 4x + 7 = 5.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Getting the sign of (-1)(-7) wrong in the determinant and writing 4x + 7 = 5.
